knowledge.purpose: Form container that wires its inputs to the platform/entities capability and emits submit. Submitted values are saved as a record in the app's own data, under the entity type the form is bound to.
useCases: Multi-step form (wizard): ONE form wraps every step; step buttons (button.action setState step) sit inside it; showSubmit only on the summary step; the confirmation shows on the formBinding success statusKey
antiPatterns: Wizard with explicit step navigation — wrap form inside panel.stepper
Single-input search — input + button is fine without a form wrapper
Wrapping only the first step of a multi-step flow in the form — fields of the later steps are never sent, the record is never written
knowledge.implementation:
Operational constraints (install, permissions, polling, read-only scope):
- Read-only data display — use data.list

Further use cases:
- Filter bar that produces a typed query

Validation: the form validates itself on submit. A missing visible field gets the browser's own message on that field; a required field in a hidden wizard step (visibleWhen) is named in an alert above the submit button, so the visitor can go back to it. Mark only the fields the brief requires as required.

jsonSchema.description: Bind to the formBindings statusKeys.loading state key (e.g. {{state.scLoading}}) — while true the submit button is locked with a spinner. The synchronous ref lock stays active regardless.
Whether the form renders its own submit button. Bind it for a multi-step flow: wrap EVERY step in this one form and show the submit only on the last step, e.g. {{state.step == 3}}. Unset = shown.

Clears every field when this turns true. Bind it to the formBindings statusKeys.success state key (e.g. {{state.scSuccess}}) so the form empties after a successful save. Only the false → true change resets.
Custom behavior/action name emitted on submit (in addition to the form:submit event).
